plain_description.what: Three versions of the model leaderboard, all built with the same judge. A is the published board. B adds a filter that skips matches where both models gave the same answer, at no new cost. C adds an extra re-judging step to break B's ties. The test compares ranking quality, judge accuracy and the number of judge calls.
plain_description.why: It asks whether the paper's leaderboard can be rebuilt more cheaply and more accurately from the changes that held up in earlier tests.
plain_description.information: It shows whether cheaper judging costs ranking quality, and whether tie-breaking actually helps the judge. Result: done. The filter cut judge calls from about 18,300 to about 10,550 with no loss in ranking quality. The honest claim is "no cost, about half the bill", not "a better board", because the confidence intervals overlap. The tie-break missed its target: +2.2 points of accuracy against a +3-point bar. It makes the judge commit to more matches, but the extra decisions are less accurate than its average. This belongs to the older question pool, which is now ruled history, not evidence.
